items.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
items.summary: An attacker tried to exploit a critical GitLab vulnerability on the Alpine Linux project's own GitLab server a week after GitLab released a fix, Alpine Linux said on 28 October. The flaw, CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS score: 10.0), can let an attacker run code on a GitLab server through a crafted regular expression in a CI configuration. Alpine found no evidence that the attack worked but cannot rule it out, so it rebuilt the server from scratch and reset every account's password. GitLab's fix is a set of patches to the Ruby that GitLab ships in its own packages and container images. Alpine's GitLab image used standard Ruby, so upgrading the server to GitLab 19.3.6 on 22 October did not fix the flaw. For anyone running GitLab on their own Ruby, built from source or in their own container image, "upgrading GitLab is not enough," Alpine said. Those servers also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12, 4.0.9 or later, and users of Alpine's alpinelinux/gitlab image need to pull 19.3.6 again. The server gitlab.alpinelinux.org hosts aports, the repository from which Alpine's packages are built. Packages built from 20 to 24 October, and the 21 October releases, came from aports changes verified against records outside GitLab, according to Alpine. Those releases include the minirootfs files that the official Alpine Docker images are built from. Alpine is extending the checks to 27 October, when it closed the server. The keys that sign its packages and releases have never been on the GitLab server.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware ESX Zero-Day to Reduce Audit Trail Visibility
items.summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Wednesday added a security flaw impacting Broadcom VMware ESX to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, after CrowdStrike revealed that it had been weaponized by a China-nexus threat actor known as Warp Panda in attacks targeting the U.S. legal sector. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-41709 (CVSS score: 2.7), an a case of insufficient logging that could permit permit a malicious actor with admin access to perform certain operations without being logged. In an advisory released in July 2026, Broadcom revealed that the issue was addressed in the following versions: VMware Cloud Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025 VMware vSphere Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025 VMware ESX ESXi80U3j-25429389 VMware Cloud Foundation 5.2.4 VMware Telco Cloud Platform ESXi80U3j-25429389 The development comes in response to CrowdStrike's 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report, which revealed that Warp Panda had exploited CVE-2026-41709 as a zero-day in early 2026 with an aim to reduce audit trail visibility.

VMware vSphere Foundation SXi-9.1.0.0-25370933 and ESXi-9.0.2.0100-25595025
VMware ESX ESXi80U3j-25429389

VMware Telco Cloud Platform ESXi80U3j-25429389

items.title: Attackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Internet-Exposed Palo Alto Networks Management Interfaces
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks on Wednesday warned that threat actors are exploiting the recently patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against publicly-accessible management interfaces. "Active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet," the network security company said in an update to its advisory. The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2), allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on systems running affected versions of PHP. The issues were patched upstream by the PHP Foundation on October 21, 2026, in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The development comes days after Israeli cybersecurity company Dream said it observed a suspected China-nexus threat actor weaponizing the flaws in conjunction with a local privilege escalation bug in the Linux kernel, tracked as Fragnesia (CVE-2026-46300, CVSS score: 7.8), to root 25 servers across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea. Among those were three systems belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated environment.

items.title: Belgium's tax agency confirms cyberattack, pulls services offline
items.summary: Belgium's finance and tax agency has pulled "several" digital services offline after a cyberattack on the organization. FOD Financiën confirmed the attack on Wednesday, saying that MyMinfin, the agency's main online tax portal, as well as other online services, are temporarily unavailable while they start the initial investigations. "This measure helps limit the risks and makes it possible to carry out the necessary technical interventions to ensure the security of our systems," it said in a public announcement. FOD Financiën added that "this has consequences for tax deadlines in the near future," referring to the October 31 extended deadline to submit tax filings for specific types of income, such as sole traders and earnings from foreign companies. The agency confirmed the deadline will be extended to November 16, by which time MyMinfin, the platform through which such filings would normally be submitted, should be back up and running. The detail offered up in the public statement reflects the early stage of the investigation; not much is known, although there is nothing to suggest data was compromised. "Data protection is a top priority for the FOD Financiën," it said. "At present, there are no indications that a data breach has occurred or that data has been compromised. This aspect is also being closely investigated and followed up. "In the meantime, a large part of our other applications remains available with full or partial functionality. We are closely monitoring the situation and doing everything we can to make the affected services available again as soon as possible." Spokesperson Francis Adyns told local news outlets that the attack was thwarted within hours, and that it was unable to gain access to applications or data. "The attack could not be sufficiently expanded within our environment to take over applications or gain access to data," he told Nieuwsblad. "Elements that were potentially infected were isolated. As a result, MyMinfin, Tax-on-web, and Biztax went offline, but the hacking was successfully stopped. "The various services must be restored in an isolated environment. This requires considerable time to realize, with the necessary caution to rule out new risks."

items.title: Hackers exploit Cisco SD-WAN flaw to deploy custom KeyDrift malware
items.summary: A newly identified advanced persistent threat (APT) group tracked as UAT-11473 was observed exploiting CVE-2026-20127, an authentication-bypass flaw in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controllers, to deploy a custom malware framework called KeyDrift. CVE-2026-20127 is a max-severity flaw that Cisco patched in February 2026, which allows remote attackers to gain privileged access to Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager and add rogue peers. UAT-8616 has exploited the vulnerability as a zero-day since at least 2023, and recent research also linked its exploitation to the Chinese Volt Typhoon state-sponsored hacking group.

items.title: Hacktivists 'Department of Peace' Leak DHS Employee Data
items.summary: The identities of more than 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, including agents working in immigration, surveillance and undercover, have been leaked online by hacktivists. "The database, from an Okta single sign-on service used by the DHS, reveals employee names, offices, contact information and assignments," said transparency group Distributed Denial of Secrets. The U.S. nonprofit said it's devoted to archiving and publishing "hacked and leaked documents in the public interest." The information, comprising over 165 megabytes of data, has been dubbed "Icepick," in reference to the heavily criticized Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. A hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace - a riposte to the Trump administration styling the Pentagon as the Department of War - said it obtained the data and shared it with Distributed Denial of Secrets and Swiss developer and hacktivist "maia arson crimew," who's designed an online search tool for the data at Icepi.cx. "This is not a comprehensive list of all DHS employees. All data is provided as-is; inaccuracies are from source data and may be reproduced," the site reads. A DHS spokesperson said the agency is "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." "We take all security threats against our employees and officers seriously and will work to ensure all are properly protected," the spokesperson said. "We will update the public when more information is available." Three DHS employees included in the leaks, contacted by Reuters confirmed that their name and contact information was legitimate.

items.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Unavailable, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 9.8, CVEs: CVE-2026-98432, Summary: A flaw in the Linux kernel's TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, affects Ubuntu, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and other Linux distributions. The kernel's own CVE team rates it 9.8 out of 10 on the CVSS scale. Anthropic said on October 27 that its AI model wrote an exploit that uses the flaw to let a remote attacker with no credentials run commands as root on Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener. As of October 29, Ubuntu and RHEL have not released a fixed kernel. Red Hat, Amazon, Oracle, and SUSE score the flaw between 5.9 and 8.1, lower than the kernel team's 9.8. The flaw is a race condition in the code that sets up new IPv4 TCP connections. It can make the kernel read memory it has already freed, a bug type known as a use-after-free. As of October 28, the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) had not added its own score and showed the kernel team's 9.8. Ubuntu's page also shows that score. Red Hat's CVE page rates the flaw Moderate, scoring it 5.9 because the race is hard to win. It says the most likely result is a kernel crash, with memory corruption possible in theory, and that "no confidentiality or integrity impact has been demonstrated." Red Hat's machine-readable advisory file, updated on October 29, lists the impact as Important and scores the flaw 8.1, with high confidentiality and integrity impact. items.title: Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches
items.summary: A massive search-hijacking campaign involving 319 Chrome extensions with a combined 13.4 million reported installations redirected users' searches through tracking servers to generate advertising revenue from Bing and Yahoo. A new report by Socket's John Tuckner expands on the researcher's April 2025 discovery of 57 Chrome extensions with 6 million users, adding 264 newly identified add-ons with another 8.7 million users. "These extensions were created by a handful of organized operators all working from the same idea: quietly take over the browser's default search engine, route every query through a suspicious proxy server, and collect partner referral payments from Yahoo or Bing under a syndication partner ID," explained Tuckner.

items.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: High, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: A flaw in Telegram for Android could be chained with two other bugs to take full control of a victim's phone through a voice call, once the victim answered, according to security startup NebuSec. The attacker needed only an ordinary Telegram account. Telegram fixed the flaw in version 12.10.4 of the app, released in late September, and NebuSec disclosed it on October 29. Combined with an information-leak bug, the flaw gives the attacker an escape from the Telegram app to Android, NebuSec co-founder and chief executive Eten Zou told The Hacker News. Adding an Android root exploit then gives full control of the phone, including its messages, microphone and camera. The flaw can be triggered in every version from 8.6.2 through 12.10.3, Zou said. Those versions came out between March 2022 and September 2026. The company confirmed it in private voice calls on ARM64-based phones and has no evidence so far that it directly affects Telegram's iOS and desktop apps or group calls. Anyone using Telegram for Android should make sure the app is on version 12.10.4 or later. The version number appears at the bottom of the app's Settings page. The flaw had no CVE identifier as of October 29. See also: https://x.com/nebusecurity/status/2115601122727702634

items.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
items.summary: Cisco released security updates to patch a denial-of-service zero-day in Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) and Threat Defense (FTD) software that attackers are exploiting to remotely crash vulnerable firewall devices. Tracked as CVE-2026-76418, this high-severity vulnerability affects devices running ASA and FTD software with configurations containing the 'webvpn' keyword and SSL VPN enabled on at least one interface. Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to trigger a denial-of-service (DoS) condition, causing the device to reload unexpectedly.

items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense Software Remote Access SSL VPN Tunnel Denial of Service Vulnerability
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: 8.6, CVEs: CVE-2026-76418, Summary: A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition. Cisco has released software updates that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability. However, there is a mitigation, which is to disable secondary authentication on any user-configured tunnel group list or on the default tunnel group, DefaultWEBVPNGroup. While this mitigation has been deployed and was proven successful in a test environment, customers should determine the applicability and effectiveness in their own environment and under their own use conditions. Customers should be aware that any workaround or mitigation that is implemented may negatively impact the functionality, performance, and/or security posture of their network based on intrinsic customer deployment scenarios and limitations. Customers should not deploy any workarounds or mitigations before first evaluating the applicability to their own environment and any impact to such environment. Cisco strongly recommends upgrading to the fixed software listed in the Fixed Software section of this advisory. Vulnerable Products This vulnerability affects Cisco devices if they are running a vulnerable release of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software or Cisco Secure FTD Software, the SSL remote access VPN login service is reachable, and secondary authentication is configured in the tunnel group scope that is described in the following sections. If the running configuration contains the webvpn keyword and SSL VPN is enabled on at least one interface, the configuration is vulnerable. Cisco has confirmed that this vulnerability does not affect the following Cisco products: Cloud-delivered Firewall (CDFW) Cloud-delivered Firewall Management Center (cdFMC) Secure Access (CSA) Secure FMC Software

items.title: Tietoturvan suunnannäyttäjä -tunnustus annettiin työstä pankkitunnuskalastelujen estämiseksi
items.summary: Traficom jakaa vuosittain tunnustuksen esimerkillisestä tietoturvaa edistävästä työstä. Tunnustus jaettiin nyt kymmenettä kertaa. Tänä vuonna tunnustuksen sai Tuomas Kaijanen OP Pohjolasta. Tuomas Kaijasen sinnikäs työ on tuottanut pankkihuijausten torjuntaa tehostavan yhteistyömallin, jonka avulla pankit, teleoperaattorit ja viranomaiset ovat onnistuneet merkittävästi vähentämään pankkitunnuskalastelun uhrimääriä. Pilotointivaihe saatiin päätökseen huhtikuussa 2025 ja seuraavaksi uutta mallia kehitetään kansalliseksi ratkaisuksi, josta hyötyy koko yhteiskunta.

items.title: Huijari ei tarvitse pankkitunnuksiasi – veloitus voi ilmestyä puhelinlaskullesi
items.summary: Poliisin tietoon on tullut uudenlainen huijaustapa, jossa rikolliset hyödyntävät matkapuhelinliittymän kautta tapahtuvaa laskutusta. Huijauksen tarkoituksena on liittää uhrin matkapuhelinliittymä maksutavaksi esimerkiksi Applen sovelluskaupan tilille. Kun huijari saa haltuunsa puhelinnumeron ja vahvistuskoodin, hän voi tehdä sovelluskaupassa ostoja, jotka veloitetaan uhrin matkapuhelinlaskulla. Uudelle huijaustavalle on tyypillistä, että huijari esiintyy uhrin ystävänä sosiaalisessa mediassa tehdyllä valeprofiililla ja pyytää tältä puhelinnumeroa sekä tämän jälkeen puhelimeen saapuvaa vahvistuskoodia. Matkapuhelinliittymän kautta tehtävien ostojen käyttöraja vaihtelee operaattoreittain noin 150–300 euron välillä kuukaudessa. Huijauksesta voi siis aiheutua uhrille useiden satojen eurojen taloudellinen vahinko. Uhri saattaa havaita huijauksen vasta tavallista suuremmasta puhelinlaskusta tai huomatessaan laskulla omituisia maksuja.

items.title: Historiallinen deepfake-tuomio – uhrin sanat pysäyttivät: ”Tuskallisen todellinen”
items.summary: Australia on antanut ensimmäisen tuomion seksuaalisen deepfake-kuvan jakamisesta. Ilman suostumusta jaettavat deepfake-pornokuvat kieltävä laki hyväksyttiin Australian parlamentissa 21. elokuuta 2024, ja se astui virallisesti voimaan 3. syyskuuta 2024. 20-vuotias mies myönsi luoneensa seksuaalisia deepfake-kuvia teini-ikäisestä tytöstä ja jakaneensa niitä eri verkkoalustoilla vuosien 2024 ja 2025 aikana, ABC News kertoo. Deepfake-kuvien levittämisen lisäksi mies myönsi syyllistyneensä myös viestisovelluksessa uhkaamiseen, häirintään ja loukkaamiseen sekä viestisovelluksen käyttämiseen henkilötietojen selvittämiseksi. Mies oli tekohetkellä 18-vuotias. Hänestä tuli ensimmäinen ihminen Australiassa, jota syytettiin vuoden 2024 lakien nojalla.

items.title: Saksan AfD-puolueen johdossa kiersi lista ”vihollisista” – joukossa suomalaisten nimiä ja osoitteita
items.summary: Saksalaisen Vaihtoehto Saksalle -puolueen (AfD) johtajien parissa on kiertänyt niin sanottu vihollislista, jolta löytyy ainakin 19 suomalaisen nimi, osoite, sähköpostiosoite ja puhelinnumero. Asia käy ilmi laajasta sähköpostivuodosta, jota Ylen verifiointitiimi on tutkinut kansainvälisen toimittajajärjestön OCCRP:n kanssa. Vuodettujen sähköpostien liitteenä on nimilista, joka on otsikoitu nimellä ”Antifan jäsenet”. Antifa on vasemmistolainen liike, joka vastustaa laitaoikeistolaista AfD:tä ja muita fasistisina pitämiään tahoja. Paraisilla asuva koulunkäynninohjaaja ja kuvittaja Amanda Österman on yksi listalle päätyneistä. – Kuulostaa vähän pelottavalta. En ole ollut aktiivinen poliittisissa ryhmissä, joten tuntuu todella vieraalta ja oudolta joutua tällaiselle listalle, Österman sanoo Ylelle. Samalla listalla on myös jutun alun videolla haastateltu Walter Lüttge. AfD:n johdon viestit ovat osa laajaa tietovuotoa, joka käsittää yli 420 000 AfD-puolueen sähköpostia ja yli 100 000 muuta dokumenttia. Hakkerit latasivat aineiston lokakuun loppupuolella internetiin. Yle osallistuu vuodetun aineiston tutkimiseen, koska AfD-puolue on merkittävä vallankäyttäjä. Lisäksi Saksan viranomaiset ovat vuosien ajan tutkineet puolueen mahdollisia yhteyksiä äärioikeistoon. Koko aineistosta löytyy yhteensä 23 suomalaisen henkilötiedot, käy ilmi Ylen selvityksestä.
